title: Python SDK: ergonomic streaming chat handler patterns for resumability and telemetry
creator: Ava Chen
description: Design and implement a set of ergonomic handler primitives in the Python SDK to make streaming chat completions resumable, observable, and easy to compose with user code. This ticket focuses on: (1) a small set of handler abstractions for event dispatch and checkpointing; (2) backpressure and retry semantics for consumer code; (3) standardized telemetry hooks (latency, partial-token counters, dropped events); and (4) examples and documentation that demonstrate common patterns (UI streaming, long-poll resumable sessions, server-side fanout).
acceptance_criteria: A minimal public API (~3 functions/classes) exists in the python SDK and is documented in the README
Handlers support explicit checkpointing and a lightweight resume token that can rehydrate stream state and resume from last committed token
Built-in backpressure semantics prevent unbounded memory growth in consumer examples (bounded queue or semaphore usage exposed as a helper)
Retry semantics implement idempotent replays where supported; non-idempotent operations have a documented guidance path
Unit and integration tests cover: normal stream flow, transient disconnect + resume, permanent failure, and duplicate-message suppression
Telemetry hooks emit token-level counters, resume attempts, and stream durations to our telemetry backend (integration test verifies events sent to mock endpoint)
Example notebooks or code samples show (a) web UI incremental rendering, (b) server-side resumable recording, and (c) a long-tail fanout consumer pattern
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Initial design kickoff; scoped to SDK primitives + examples; proto API sketched in design doc (see links).
2026-02-24: Spike completed for resume token format: small JSON with model, request_id, last_event_id, kv_cache_hint; landed prototype in feature branch.
2026-03-02: Implementation of StreamHandler base class started; added event types and simple dispatch loop; initial tests for normal flow passing locally.
2026-03-08: Added bounded-queue helper + semaphore-based backpressure primitive; integrated with example web UI sample; observed improved memory stability under high concurrency.
2026-03-11: Telemetry adapter hook implemented; wiring to mock telemetry backend for CI integration tests in progress.
2026-03-12: Opened draft PR for review (see links) and requested Design/PM feedback on resume UX and default checkpoint frequency.
decisions: Keep public surface minimal: provide StreamHandler, ResumableCheckpoint, and backpressure_helpers; avoid exposing internal queue state.
Resume token will be a compact base64-encoded JSON to avoid leaking long internals; include an HMAC slot for future integrity checks (not required for MVP).
Default checkpoint policy: time+token hybrid (checkpoint at 2s intervals or every 128 tokens, whichever comes first); configurable by user via ResumableCheckpoint.params.

Retries will attempt a single transparent resume with exponential backoff (100ms -> 500ms) for network blips; multi-retry semantics will be explicit helpers to avoid surprising duplicate side-effects.
Telemetry will be opt-in at SDK init and use a single hook interface so customers can wire to Prometheus/Datadog/OTel.
review_feedback: PM (Ravi Patel) — please add a short migration note for existing users of streaming iterator APIs and call out breaking changes (if any).
Design (Maya Alvarez) — UI sample should include token-level patches to show partial tokens flushing; suggested an additional example for high-latency mobile networks.
Security (Liam O'Malley) — check resume token leakage vectors in logs; add guidance to redact tokens in stdout logs and add optional token encryption using customer KMS in Private deployments.
Eng (Mateo Ruiz) — consider a pluggable deduplication strategy for server fanout scenarios; naive dedupe by event id is acceptable for MVP.
